writeup.p: C19 is the client's reply to S48PacketResourcePackSend: a hash String plus an Action enum (SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED, DECLINED, FAILED_DOWNLOAD, ACCEPTED). Vanilla sends ACCEPTED when the user confirms the download prompt, then SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED or FAILED_DOWNLOAD after the download resolves. Servers that require a pack gate features or membership on the ACCEPTED reply.

The bundled 1.8.9 server handler, handleResourcePackStatus, is an empty method; decline kicks and pack-required logic are plugin territory. Client-side, NetHandlerPlayClient.handleResourcePackSend downloads the pack and reports the outcome through C19, and the download itself is a URL fetch with no scheme validation in vanilla, which is the hole the security modules patch.

Two families. (1) Security: Rise 6.x ResourcePackCheck (a SecurityFeature) and Tenacity's AntiExploit module and Enhancements utility intercept S48, validate the URL scheme, block level:// traversal and non-http hosts, and answer C19 with FAILED_DOWNLOAD so the server's state machine stays consistent. (2) Disabler: Rise 5.99's c19 mode sends C19 with an empty hash and ACCEPTED to unlock pack-gated features without downloading. LiquidSense Dev adds a third family: a mixin on NetHandlerPlayClient's handleResourcePack performs the same scheme guard as family (1), answering C19 with FAILED_DOWNLOAD and the real hash. November Recode 2.0 only registers C19 in its Lua scripting id map (0x19).

The level:// protocol reads files from the server's save directory; a malicious pack URL with path traversal is a server-to-client file disclosure vector, which is exactly what both security implementations check for. The empty-hash ACCEPTED spoof exploits plugins that match the hash against the last S48; a strict plugin sees the mismatch, a sloppy one unlocks the feature. Because the vanilla server handler is empty, declined packs never kick in vanilla; the whole battlefield is plugin-side.

overview: The resource-pack handshake reply. Security layers in Rise 6.x and Tenacity block malicious pack URLs and answer FAILED_DOWNLOAD, while Rise 5.99's Disabler spoofs ACCEPTED with an empty hash to unlock pack-gated features without downloading anything. LiquidSense Dev ships the same scheme guard as a mixin on the vanilla handler.
server_handling: handleResourcePackStatus is an empty no-op in the bundled 1.8.9 sources; pack-required kicks and feature gating live in plugins that read the Action. The client handler performs an unvalidated URL fetch, making S48 the disclosure vector and C19 the acknowledgment channel.
protocol_notes: String hash + VarInt enum action. The hash must echo the one from the triggering S48 for strict plugins. The enum order on the wire is SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED=0, DECLINED=1, FAILED_DOWNLOAD=2, ACCEPTED=3. C19 is only meaningful after an S48; a serverbound C19 with a hash the server never sent is the spoof signature.
anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures C19. Anti-exploit plugins validate pack URLs server-side and match C19 hashes against their own S48 log; an empty-hash ACCEPTED or a FAILED_DOWNLOAD for a pack the server never sent is the detectable pattern. The security modules' FAILED_DOWNLOAD replies are indistinguishable from a genuine failed download, which is what makes them stealthy.

modules.name: ResourcePackCheck
modules.purpose: Block malicious level:// resource packs and reply FAILED_DOWNLOAD to keep the server state machine consistent.
modules.how_it_works: As a SecurityFeature it intercepts S48, validates scheme and path (no traversal, must end in /resources.zip), and on violation sends C19 FAILED_DOWNLOAD via sendNoEvent and cancels the pack.
modules.vanilla_hook: SecurityFeature packet handle, no module toggle.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The FAILED_DOWNLOAD reply matches what a genuine failed download looks like, so pack-gated servers see a normal failure rather than a refusal.
modules.variations: Identical SecurityFeature in Rise 6.1.30. LiquidSense Dev implements the same scheme guard as a mixin on NetHandlerPlayClient (see the resource pack guard entry).

modules.name: AntiExploit
modules.purpose: Block malicious resource packs (and other exploit packets) at the receive layer, answering C19 FAILED_DOWNLOAD for blocked packs.
modules.how_it_works: The PacketReceiveEvent handler rejects non-http/https/level schemes and level:// URLs with traversal or a missing /resources.zip suffix, cancels the S48 and replies C19 with the pack's real hash.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Uses the real S48 hash in the reply, which makes the FAILED_DOWNLOAD fully consistent with the last pack the server sent; undetectable as a block.
modules.variations: Tenacity's Enhancements utility performs the same scheme check and C19 reply globally, outside any module toggle.

modules.name: Disabler (pack accept spoof)
modules.purpose: Spoof a resource-pack acceptance with an empty hash to unlock pack-gated server features.
modules.how_it_works: The c19 disabler mode sends C19 with an empty hash string and ACCEPTED via sendPacketWithoutEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: A strict server matches the hash against its own S48 log and sees the empty hash; a sloppy one unlocks the gated features. No anti-cheat involvement.
modules.variations: No other client in the corpus spoofs ACCEPTED; the other implementations block instead of accept.

modules.name: Enhancements (protocol guard)
modules.purpose: Globally reject non-http/https/level pack URLs and answer FAILED_DOWNLOAD outside any module.
modules.how_it_works: The static utility validates the S48 URL scheme, sends C19 FAILED_DOWNLOAD with the real hash for bad schemes and throws URISyntaxException to abort the vanilla download.
modules.vanilla_hook: S48 receive interception via the utility's integration point.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Same stealth profile as AntiExploit: the reply is a consistent FAILED_DOWNLOAD with the correct hash.
modules.variations: AntiExploit is the user-facing module; Enhancements is the always-on guard.

modules.name: MixinNetHandlerPlayClient (resource pack guard)
modules.purpose: Block malicious level:// resource packs at the vanilla handler and reply C19 FAILED_DOWNLOAD to keep the server state machine consistent.
modules.how_it_works: @Inject on handleResourcePack HEAD, cancellable: parse the S48 URL scheme, require http/https/level, and for level:// reject traversal (..) or a path not ending in /resources.zip. On URISyntaxException it logs, sends C19(hash, FAILED_DOWNLOAD) through netManager, and cancels the vanilla handler so the download never starts.
modules.vanilla_hook: @Inject on NetHandlerPlayClient.handleResourcePack; netManager.sendPacket for the reply.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The FAILED_DOWNLOAD carries the real S48 hash, indistinguishable from a genuine download failure; same stealth profile as the Rise 6.x SecurityFeature.
modules.variations: The same mixin class also overwrites handleConfirmTransaction and fires EntityMovementEvent, which is why it appears in the S32 and S14 impl pages.

general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent on S48PacketResourcePackSend (Tenacity), SecurityFeature handle (Rise 6.x), direct send for the spoof (Rise 5.99).
client_variations: Rise 6.x answers via PacketUtil.sendNoEvent; Tenacity via mc.getNetHandler().addToSendQueue or networkManager.sendPacket; Rise 5.99 via sendPacketWithoutEvent. PingSpoofComponent also holds C19 in its blink tuple in both Rise 6.x builds. November Recode 2.0 registers C19 in its LuaEventPacket scripting id map (0x19) but ships no pack-handling module.
